phase-plan.purpose: Replace the next ad hoc JSON editing step with schema-driven forms and a fresh Asset Explorer surface that can create, browse, search, and analyze authored assets, then extend that same surface so Escape the Dungeon canonical pack schemas can be seeded/imported and edited through the same workflow.
phase-plan.scope: In scope: `react-jsonschema-form` integration, a new docs-site Asset Explorer route, project/form selection, asset CRUD create/update flows bound to selected schemas, simple x/y/z numeric plotting, and the first game-specific canonical schema seeding/import path for Escape the Dungeon. Out of scope: auth hardening, delete flows, diff/review gates, and full publish governance.

file.description: New top-level route for the reset asset-authoring experience.
Main asset CRUD and schema-form workspace built over project/custom-schema/project-data APIs.
Simple scatter3d view over selected assets using chosen numeric leaf paths.
Content-app overview should link to Asset Explorer as the preferred asset-authoring surface.
Add `react-jsonschema-form` packages so forms come from schemas instead of another custom editor widget layer.

task.description: Install `react-jsonschema-form` and stand up a fresh Asset Explorer page that binds selected project forms to project data records.
Add analytical viewing for selected form collections with search, asset detail, and simple x/y/z plotting over discovered numeric paths.

Document the planning redirect away from `50-12` Space Explorer verification and into the phase 63 Asset Explorer lane, then narrow the first forms/data support to Escape the Dungeon canonical schemas and imported pack documents.

decision.summary: The next authoring surface should be a fresh Asset Explorer rather than another extension of the old all-in-one content page or Space Explorer.
decision.impact: Phase 63 becomes the honest critical path for editor work; schema-driven forms and asset collection views are now the baseline for future richer CRUD, review, and delivery flows.

decision.summary: For the first slice, assets are stored in existing project-data records and linked to a selected schema via `targetId === schemaId`.
decision.impact: This avoids a new persistence model tonight while still enabling schema-backed asset creation, search, and visualization immediately.

decision.summary: The schema-form/editor work should stop pretending to be generic and should support Escape the Dungeon first by deriving item-level forms from the game's canonical pack schemas and editing imported pack data in place.
decision.impact: Phase 63 remains aligned with the playable game: the editor now grows from the same contracts and data packs the engine and KAPLAY demo consume, while broader productization stays deferred.

suggestion.gap: Current phase 63 wording names schema forms abstractly but does not call out the new Asset Explorer product surface, analytical collection view, or the narrower Escape the Dungeon-first schema/data scope.
suggestion.proposal: Amend ROADMAP/STATE/task wording so phase 63 explicitly treats Asset Explorer as the schema-driven CRUD and analysis surface for Escape the Dungeon canonical assets first, with auth/review gates following later.
